<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata/src/serializers/typescript-serializer.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **139** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json beac7980267a361c5979ca7aa75c034624955af0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

## Contract review

Served-tier: 61/61 `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2f378ec5cfda272f20cdc961c084f27d660b37ce`

Isolated at-tier reviewer subagent, run by the `domain:spec` seat-4 session on the maintainer's instruction in that session (「帮我处理」, with the landing route chosen there); every one of its 61 transcript turns served at the tier the constant names. Adopted by the seat 2026-09-24T05:39Z. The record below is the reviewer's, unedited except the two header lines. The reviewer's own `Served-tier:` line declared a lower tier than the transcript shows; the seat replaced it with the transcript measurement.


### ① Derived judgments

1. The change, verified at the ref. `git diff --stat 8490127962834a125239ae85d9e6a88c0386896c refs/review/pr-19919` (merge-base to head): 5 files, +143/−6, identical to `pulls/19919/files`. The one declaration moved is `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts:6327` at refs/review/pr-19919: `export type ViewMetadata = z.input over (typeof VIEW_METADATA_MEMBERS)[ViewMetadataBranch]` (origin/main `:6310` had `z.input over typeof ViewMetadataSchema`). `ViewMetadataParsed` (`:6329`) is a context line, unchanged. `ViewMetadataSchema` (`:6020-6037`), `VIEW_METADATA_MEMBERS` (`:5615-5624`) and the preprocess are untouched, so the runtime accept set cannot have moved. RIGHT against the card, which asked for exactly "the input of the post-preprocess union (the members the union runs)".

2. Derivable and honest. `VIEW_METADATA_MEMBERS` is `as const satisfies Record of ViewMetadataBranch to z.ZodTypeAny` (`:5624`), so its values keep concrete types; `lazySchema` is typed `T extends z.ZodTypeAny, (factory: () to T): T` (`packages/spec/src/shared/lazy-schema.ts:21`), so `z.input` over the indexed union distributes to the four members' inputs. The schema is built from the same record (`:6026` maps `VIEW_METADATA_BRANCHES` over it), so member list and type cannot drift. The card's premise (preprocess input is unknown; members cast to `z.ZodTypeAny` at `:6035`) holds at both refs.

3. Exactly the runtime accept set? No, and no TS type can be, and the PR says so in the TSDoc (`:6320-6325`) and the changeset. Wider than the door: refinements (`containerHasAView` on the container member `:5538` region, `assertViewIdentity` in the preprocess `:6029`, `checkListViewCalendarVisualization` `:5573`) and mixed-member literals (container member all-optional; TS judges an object literal's keys against the union as a whole). Narrower than the door: `stripViewConsoleDecorations` removes row ids before any member judges, and strip-mode members drop undeclared keys, so those bodies parse but their literals are TS2353. The PR measured the exclusive-union alternative and rejected it with a reason (four platform-written PUT bodies would be refused). Not a defect against the card. The 17/3/8/16 matrix is the author's measurement; I did not re-run it (no local gate re-runs), but each class's direction follows from the schema text above.

4. Pin is weight-bearing and CI-judged. `packages/spec/src/ui/view-metadata-type.test.ts:61-66` carries three `@ts-expect-error` directives (unknown, undeclared key, scalar), one body per member typed through the published name (`:33-49`), and a coverage assertion against `VIEW_METADATA_BRANCHES` (`:71-73`). The file sits inside `tsconfig.test.json` `include: ["src/**/*"]` and has no entry in `packages/spec/test-typecheck-debt.json` (grep for `view-metadata-type` exits 1; ledger byte-identical between origin/main and the PR ref), so an unused directive (TS2578) reds the gate. CI at head: `Type Check · workspace` job 107341254326 (head_sha 2f378ec5cf…), step "Type check workspace packages" success; log shows `@objectstack/spec:typecheck` running `tsc --noEmit && pnpm check:scripts-typecheck && pnpm check:test-typecheck`, then `check:test-typecheck: OK — @objectstack/spec's test layer compiles under packages/spec/tsconfig.test.json; 53 file(s) / 255 error(s) / 142 pinned signature(s) held`. With the new file in that program, that green line is CI-side proof the narrowing fired; the PR's ablation control (revert the line, 3x TS2578 at 61/63/65) is consistent.

5. Consumers. `git grep -n -w ViewMetadata refs/review/pr-19919 -- ':!packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts'`: no annotation consumer outside the new test — only comments (`packages/metadata/src/serializers/typescript-serializer.ts:31,34`), the test docblock, two changesets, `packages/metadata/README.md:77`, and the baseline rows `api-surface/ui.json:428`, `export-origins/ui.json:414`. objectui at the pin (`.objectui-sha` at origin/main = `62597c588072636e9c30ea35b3d89b1e46fd765d`): `git grep -n -w ViewMetadata` exits 1, `ViewMetadataParsed` exits 1; control grep `ViewMetadataSchema|VIEW_METADATA_MEMBERS|diagnoseViewMetadata` hits 11 files, so the negative reading is valid. All four Type Check lanes at head are success with head_sha 2f378ec5cf… (source gates 107341254519, workspace 107341254326, debt ledger 107341254648, consumer gates 107341254656). `Console Pin Gate` was skipped at head (ci.yml `console` path filter: `.objectui-sha`, `scripts/build-console.sh`, …; none touched), so objectui was not built against this head in CI; with zero references at the pin nothing there can break.

6. Does the api-surface baseline record it? No, by design. `packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json:428` `"ViewMetadata (type)"` identical at both refs; `packages/spec/scripts/build-api-surface.ts` header: one `name (kind)` row per declared kind, and the signature hash "prints a type REFERENCE and does not expand it"; `api-surface-signatures.json` covers only `defineX` factories, none of which names `ViewMetadata`. AGENTS.md `:750`: the snapshot "records that an export exists, never what it resolves to". Consumer-gates step "Check @objectstack/spec public API surface" success. The changeset is therefore the only record of the narrowing, which is what the PR states.

7. Collision with #19920: none. #19920 names `ViewMetadataParsed` (two lines below), `InlineAction`, `AssembledViewArtifact`, `JoinedReportBlock`; this diff changes none (view.zod.ts hunk is `:6309-6327` only). The changeset states `ViewMetadataParsed` is unchanged and still `unknown`. #19920 is `pm:blocked` Blocked-by #19871 with triage saying do not fold it into #19919; honoured.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/view-metadata-type-not-unknown.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`; line-leading `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; a BREAKING banner naming the affected party (TypeScript code that annotates with `ViewMetadata`); one adr-0087 HTML-comment marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with its why. The PR body carries the same line-leading `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; the claim's provisional `Clause-②: no` is declared superseded.
- AGENTS.md `:1084-1085`: declaration is `yes|no` plus at most one arm; `(narrowing)` is BREAKING; `no (widening)` malformed. `no (narrowing)` is legal and honest here: no new key on a published payload (runtime accept set unchanged), a published TYPE narrows. Level: `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` header (launch window: "a breaking change ships as minor … the mandatory information carriers are the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 disposition") makes `minor` correct; `patch` would misgrade a breaking change, `major` is refused.
- Disposition: `type-surface-only` (ADR-0087 addendum 2026-08-30, `docs/adr/0087-…md:717-871`) is closed by predicate 2 (diff touches `packages/spec/**`) and predicate 3 (a `*.zod.ts` moved); the addendum's closing paragraph itself says a spec-bumping case "is not a member of this class". `registered` would put a prescription in a ledger `objectstack migrate meta` cannot project. `no-migration-prescription` is the remaining honest category, and the marker says why. Nothing authorable is removed or renamed, so no FROM to TO block is owed.
- CI at head, `Check Changeset` job 107341251773 log: `check-adr-0087-registration: 1 declared-breaking changeset(s) … [BREAKING+clause-②-narrowing] not-required (no-migration-prescription)`; `check-changeset-no-major`: "This diff introduces no major bump" and `LEVEL AXIS: this PR declares clause-② no (narrowing) … direction arm: narrowing — a BREAKING change; during the launch window it ships minor`; `check-empty-changeset`: no merge-base changeset modified or deleted.
- Judgment: correctly declared at every layer.

### ③ Boundary flags

BLOCKING
- Published prose made false and not corrected: `packages/metadata/README.md:77` at refs/review/pr-19919 still reads "`view` (its `ViewMetadata` type is `unknown`)". `packages/metadata/package.json` `files` is `["dist","README.md","CHANGELOG.md"]`, so this sentence ships in the `@objectstack/metadata` tarball; after this PR the parenthetical is false, and it steers a consumer toward exactly the assumption the changeset's BREAKING banner warns against. The PR corrected the same sentence's two siblings (`typescript-serializer.ts:27-36` comment, `typescript-serializer-annotation.test.ts:15` docblock) but not the published one; the docs-drift bot on the PR warned that pages documenting `typescript-serializer.ts` were NOT COVERED by its run. Remedy is one clause (the reason `view` stays unannotated is that `ViewMetadata` is no longer the bound schema's `z.input`, as the serializer comment now says); comment-only for `@objectstack/metadata`, no second changeset needed.

Non-blocking
- Files outside the claim's named surface: `packages/metadata/src/serializers/typescript-serializer.ts` (comment only) and its `-annotation.test.ts` (one docblock word). Declared as deviations in the os-dev report; the claim anticipated the serializer comment "becomes a reader of the fix". No runtime change; metadata typecheck and tests green.
- `.changeset/19852-typescript-serializer-per-type-annotation.md:11` (pending on origin/main, compiles into the same CHANGELOG release) still says "`ViewMetadata` is `unknown`". Editing another PR's pending changeset is the route-0 "deliberate correction" class in the `Check Changeset` step (written confirmation, check stays red), so leaving it is defensible; the two entries will contradict each other in one release note unless the maintainer rules otherwise. A decision, not a defect.
- The card's second half ("add the case to whatever gate is meant to catch exported types that collapse to unknown") and triage's same direction have no carrier: the PR's acceptance notes say "carrier: none", #19920 only mentions the census as a possible gate. `check:exported-any` reads ZodType-of-any annotations only (AGENTS.md `:750-753`; consumer-gates step "Check no exported spec type resolves to any" green while the four #19920 sites still resolve to unknown). Worth its own card.
- The dispatch expected `check:api-surface` to record the change; measured, it cannot (①.6). The PR states this rather than hand-editing a baseline. Correct handling.
- `Console Pin Gate` skipped at head by path filter, so "pinned sibling still compiles" rests on grep evidence, not a build (①.5).
- Declared process deviations: the empty-branch probe push was a bare `git push`, not via write-pace; `origin/main` had moved 2 commits at open and was not merged (now 10+, none touching `packages/spec` or `packages/metadata`; PR reads `mergeable: true, clean`). Neither affects the diff.
- Commit trailers on `aa5156d9de…` and `2f378ec5cf…` carry `Claude-Session:` and the model-free `Co-authored-by: Claude` pair; no model identifier in title, body, changeset or comments. PR is `draft: true`, no auto-merge, no dev-written labels: consistent with the governed-surface stop rule.
- Nit: the PR body cites objectui `origin/main` as `544ecba`; my fetched objectui `origin/main` is `62597c58…` (the pin). Zero references either way; not weight-bearing.
